messages:
maria-support: FYI customer X reported sudden increase in 5xx + timeouts for hosted inference endpoints ~11:15 PST. Getting a bunch of gateway timeouts and 'request rejected: queue depth exceeded'.
kevin-oncall: seeing alerts too. P95 latency spikes from 120ms -> 2.4s and tail 504s. Any recent config or rollout?
sam-platform: no rollout in prod clusters at that time. Autoscaler shows no node changes. I see continuous-batcher queue depth climbing on pool gpux-az3.
olga-sre: attaching quick grep of logs from gateway (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T18:14:58Z gateway INFO accept request tenant=acme id=... queue_len=120 depth_limit=128
2026-03-17T18:15:01Z batching WARN enqueue failed tenant=acme err=queue_full
2026-03-17T18:15:03Z runtime ERROR request timeout id=... upstream=continuous-batcher p99=2.1s
2026-03-17T18:15:04Z gateway ERROR reject tenant=acme reason=queue_depth_exceeded
```
kevin-oncall: queue_len 120 near depth_limit 128 — looks like a sharp tenant-local spike. Is this tenant using large seq requests or long KV cache misses?
tina-runtime: customer traffic pattern shows many concurrent short requests with long generation windows (context length 8k) which keeps KV alive and prevents evictions. Batcher can't compact them into efficient micro-batches, causing backlog.
maria-support: customer says they had a traffic burst from a nightly job and also enabled debug embeddings. Could be correlated. Customer requests repro steps so we should give them clear mitigation.
sam-platform: immediate mitigation options: 1) increase tenant queue depth for acme (temporal) 2) divert tenant to a cheaper model variant with lower memory use 3) enable short-circuit fallback to hostless small model. Which is cheapest/fastest?
olga-sre: Increasing queue depth helps but risks tail amplification. Prefer diverting to model-variant with smaller kv footprint. I can patch routing policy to route new requests to model:rw-3-small for that tenant. Need sign-off.
kevin-oncall: do it. Also limit request concurrency per API key to 30 for the tenant while we stabilize. Add a 30s global client timeout as a safety net.
deploy-bot: @olga-sre queued routing change to canary for tenant=acme on pool gpux-az3. Started at 18:18:12Z.
tina-runtime: after routing change we see queue depth drop to 20 and 5xxs fall off, p95 back to ~140ms. Still watch KV cache churn metrics though.
maria-support: customer confirmed degraded errors are gone and latency improved. They want root cause and long-term fix.
olga-sre: suspected root cause: tenant burst + long-context requests holding KV cache entries => continuous-batching queues inflate because requests not completing quickly. With depth configured ~128 we hit local saturation and gateway began rejecting. Long-term fixes: sensible tenant-level concurrency limits, autoscale batcher slots by observed longseq ratio, or enforce per-request length throttles.
kevin-oncall: opened follow-up ticket INF-7842: "Tenant KV-hold spikes cause queue saturation - autoscale/telemetry improvements" with proposed actions: telemetry alert for longseq ratio > 15%, dynamic per-tenant queue caps, and routing fallback policies. Assign to eng-runtime.
maria-support: sent postmortem note to customer and suggested temporary knobs they can use (smaller model, staggered cron, request concurrency cap). They appreciated quick mitigation.
customer-bot: Thanks team — saw immediate improvement. Will stagger their nightly job and test smaller model variant this week.
kevin-oncall: closing incident channel after 1h watch. If p95 spikes again re-open. :thumbsup:
